task: T04 of the SmartTube AI-subtitle plan: one vertical loop where fake translations drive the three display modes through a single write entry to the subtitle view. Judge these claims about write entries, re-entrancy, fallback and clearing before the scheduler and UI work build on them.

checks.claim: SubtitleManager has exactly one path that hands cues to the view, and composed text never re-enters the original-text normalization.
A translation arriving or a mode changing only recomposes the current frame and cannot change the original text state or trigger an additional original-text processing pass.
An empty original frame clears the view even when translations for the previous frame are still cached.
checks.evidence:
compose():
  if (mOriginalLines.isEmpty()) { return Collections.emptyList(); }   // checked before any mode handling
  ... mode switch below
Tests: emptyOriginalFrameClearsTheScreenInEveryMode iterates all three modes with a cached translation and asserts an empty result; SubtitleManagerTest.emptyCueUpdateClearsTheView asserts the last write is an empty list and the stored originals are empty.

checks.claim: A missing, blank or out-of-range translation falls back to the original line, and the bilingual mode never leaves a separator or placeholder behind.
Switching display modes is a pure recomposition: it cannot reorder, duplicate or lose the original, and switching back yields the same text as before.
checks.evidence:
compose() is a pure function of (mOriginalLines, mTranslations, mMode, mSourceSameAsTarget) and allocates a new list each call; setMode only stores a valid mode value (unknown values ignored).
Test cycles TRANSLATION_ONLY -> ORIGINAL_ONLY -> BILINGUAL and asserts [你好], [Hello], [Hello\n你好] respectively, with getOriginalLines() still ["Hello"].
